message:
Prepare the update. Reply with {"messages": [...], "revised_schedule": [...], "volunteer_tasks": [...]} as in the ripple-contracts skill. Do NOT create files: Ripple builds the .ics and .csv itself.
- One message per affected group (effect "inform", "resize" or the disruption origin); "group" = the group id. Say only what changed for that group. status "draft".
- "to": the address of a single person (see the attached people.csv), otherwise a short description like "40 workshop participants".
- "actions": the recovery checklist for the organizer team, 3 to 8 items, most urgent first: {"title", "description", "owner" (a role or team named in the files, e.g. "Volunteer lead", "Organizer", "Caterer"), "deadline" (a time or day taken from the plan, never invented), "priority" ("high"|"medium"|"low")}. Include confirming every item of the chosen option's "to_confirm" list.
- "revised_schedule": every schedule item or commitment whose time or place changes: {"id": node id, "start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM", "place": "..."}. Empty list if nothing moves.

messages.subject: Your workshop time has changed
messages.body:
Hello Speaker 2,

Because your train is running about 2 hours late, your workshop (10:00-11:00, room B) will not start at its original time. We are proposing to swap it with another session that can start at 10:00. We will confirm the new room and slot with you before anything is final. Please let us know if you are able to travel and whether this swap works for you.

Thank you for your flexibility.

messages.subject: Change to the 10:00 workshop
messages.body:
Hello,

The 10:00-11:00 workshop by Speaker 2 is being moved. We are proposing to swap it with another session that starts at 10:00. The room and the exact session are being confirmed and we will share them as soon as they are final. Please keep an eye on your inbox for the update.

The skill references `reference.md` for the exact shape. Let me read it.

The user asked for `actions` as part of the output, and no `files` (Ripple builds them). I'll produce the JSON now. Key grounding points:

- Speaker 2's email comes from people.csv. The workshop participants have no address, so I use the described form "40 workshop participants".
- The "to_confirm" items become actions.
- The swap session is not identified in the files, so `revised_schedule` lists only what is known: the workshop by Speaker 2 is moved, but its new time/place is not confirmed. Since the new slot and room are unconfirmed, I'll record the moved item with the delayed time window it would occupy and a place marked as to be confirmed, rather than inventing a room.
- Volunteer tasks are limited to the file's roles; I include none that aren't grounded in the plan, so I leave that list empty except for the confirmation work by the organizer.

Note on the room: the scenario lists "room B" at 10:00-11:00 as the target slot, and the schedule attribute says the smaller amphitheatre (220 seats, to confirm). I'll reflect that as the place to confirm.
